title: A supplied tensor edge has its induced module adjunction
statement: Let $e$ be a ringed tensor edge [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation]. Composing its inverse-image ring identification with its structural ring homomorphism gives ring data $d$ on the same geometric adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-ring-data]. There are an induced module lift $m$ of $d$, an adjunction $a:e^*\dashv m_*$, and a natural isomorphism $t:e_*\cong m_*$ from the edge's supplied right adjoint. The Hom bijection of $a$, after the lift's underlying-sheaf identification, is the geometric Hom bijection applied after the canonical scalar insertion of $e$. Moreover $\eta_e;t_{e^*}=\eta_a$ and $e^*(t);\epsilon_a=\epsilon_e$, so this isomorphism preserves the supplied adjunction.

lean.statement:
theorem RingedTensorEdge.inducedModuleAdjunction
    {Y X : RingedTensorCorner.{u, w}} (e : RingedTensorEdge Y X) :
    ∃ m : e.ringData.Modules,
    ∃ am : e.pullback ⊣ m.modules,
    ∃ t : e.pushforward ≅ m.modules,
      (∀ (M : Y.mateModules) (H : X.mateModules) (v : e.pullback.obj M ⟶ H),
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _ ⋙
          sheafCompose Y.topology (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat)).map
            (am.homEquiv M H v) ≫ m.underlying.hom.app H =
          e.adjunction.homEquiv _ _ (e.insertion M ≫
            (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _ ⋙
              sheafCompose X.topology (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat)).map v)) ∧
      (∀ M, e.moduleAdjunction.unit.app M ≫ t.hom.app (e.pullback.obj M) =
        am.unit.app M) ∧
      (∀ H, e.pullback.map (t.hom.app H) ≫ am.counit.app H =
        e.moduleAdjunction.counit.app H)
